name: blackswan-overnight
description: The OVERNIGHT-vs-INTRADAY return decomposition (Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019; Cliff-Cooper-Gulen): (nearly) all of the equity premium is earned OVERNIGHT (close→open) while the intraday (open→close) component is flat-to-negative. Tested as the tradeable long-overnight / short-intraday SPREAD (daily return = overnight − intraday) on SPY (its equity home) and BTC (24/7 crypto). The catch is COST: capturing the overnight leg is a round-trip EVERY day (buy at close, sell at open; reverse for the intraday short), so the spread pays TWO flips per bar. Uses the on-disk OHLC (price_open + close); the leakage surface is ALIGNMENT — overnight pairs open[t] with close[t-1] (mutation-proven). signal=overnight is the published direction, overnight_inverse the mirror. Decider is DSR-deflated oos_sharpe net of the two-flip cost. DATA: etfs/SPY-1d-*.json + binance/BTCUSDT-1d-*.json (both carry price_open).

universe.description: spy = the S&P 500 ETF (the overnight premium's equity home); btc = Bitcoin (24/7; the open/close split is a UTC-midnight convention).

signal.description: overnight = long the overnight component / short the intraday (the published direction); overnight_inverse = exact negation (mirror control). An unknown value is refused.

transaction_fee.description: Per-flip fee; the spread pays TWO flips per day (~0.2% round trip daily), the term that decides whether the real gross overnight premium survives net.

walk_forward_window.description: Which out-of-sample year is ACCOUNTED (2018-2024 so both SPY and BTC have OHLC). A real overnight edge must clear DSR-Sharpe net of cost in a MAJORITY of these 7 years.

seed.description: Contract conformance only — deterministic, not swept.
